newsitem.title: UK: NWE gas oil strong, barges frozen by high prices.
newsitem.headline: NWE gas oil strong, barges frozen by high prices.

text.p: NWE gas oil added to last week's gains on Monday, carried higher by strength in the soon to expire September gas oil contract and concerns over tight supply in the barge market, traders said. The September IPE contract, which expires on Thursday, was trading at $221.50 a tonne at 1213 GMT.
Prompt heating oil barge premiums were quoted at Sept IPE +$4/+$5, fob ARA. Further out, second half premiums were put at Oct IPE +50 cents/+$1.75 a tonne.
Players said the market had been paralysed by the high outright levels.

"Buyers are not coming in at these levels. I think a lot of people will wait until after the expiry to see if the market calms down," one trader said. "We may see a few people forced to come in ahead of the expiry but those who don't need prompt supply will keep out," another trader said.
On the cargoes market, traders saw premiums remaining firm throughout the week.
German heating oil cargoes were talked at Oct IPE +$6/+$7 a tonne with many players predicting premiums will strengthen as Germany's pre-winter heating oil demand gets into full swing.
